pages.text: A rocket is glued blocks around a Rocket Station. It needs thrusters, fuel in fluid tanks, a seat and Rocket Controls. Trips to planets also need an Interplanetary Navigator.

pages.title: Rocket Station
pages.text: Picks the destination, assembles the rocket and shows fuel, thruster and heat needs. Built around a $(l:stars/stellar_core)Stellar Core$(/l).

pages.title: Rocket Thruster
pages.text: How many you need depends on the rocket's weight and gravity at both ends. Built from a Combustion Chamber, titanium plates and a Create Propeller.

Fuel must sit in fluid tanks on the rocket. Accepted: Liquid Hydrogen, Hydrogen, Methane, Hydrocarbon, Biofuel, and TFMG diesel, gasoline, kerosene and naphtha. Amount depends on gravity at each end and the distance. See $(l:industry/tfmg_oil)Oil$(/l).
pages.title: Fuel

pages.text: Hydrocarbon is made by heated mixing of Carbon with Sodium or a Sodium Catalyst. Carbon comes from compacting coal with heat, or from a planet's air. Hydrogen and Oxygen come from the Electrolysis Machine. Check JEI for each.
pages.title: Making fuel
Computer Rack
pages.text: Holds Targeting Computers, which find better trajectories and cut fuel cost.

Atmosphere friction heats a rocket. Heat shielding goes up by adding metallic blocks anywhere on it. Northstar groups them in tiers: titanium and iron, then Martian steel, then tungsten. The station lists supported blocks.
pages.title: Heat shielding

pages.text: Sit at the Rocket Controls and press jump to start the launch sequence, jump again to cancel. Hold the slow key on descent. Landings aim at a Rocket Waypoint, recorded by using the atlas on it. Super Glue holds the rocket together.
pages.title: Launching
Rocket Controls
pages.text: Required to launch and steer. Without them the station reports no controls attached.

pages.title: Rocket Waypoint
pages.text: Marks landing coordinates. Use a Space Atlas on it to save the position.

pages.title: Auto-Landing Station
pages.text: Lands the rocket safely on its own.
